subject: Hosted API evaluation & next steps (quickstart, endpoints, rate limits)
messages:
From: Liam O'Reilly <liam@fintech.co>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@fintech.co>
Date: 2026-02-20T15:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Demo earlier today — follow-up questions

Thanks for the demo earlier — it was helpful to see the latency numbers. A couple of quick follow-ups from our side as we think about an evaluation: 

- We're a small team but expect bursty traffic during month-end reconciliation runs.
- Curious whether we should start on Hosted API or go straight to Dedicated capacity — our main concerns are throughput and data isolation.
- Can you share a quickstart (curl examples / endpoints) and an outline of rate limits for the Hosted API?

Also looping in Sara (engineering lead) — she'll own the technical evaluation.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Reilly
Head of Platform
Fintech Co

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam@fintech.co>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@fintech.co>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-21T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Demo earlier today — follow-up questions

Hi Liam / Sara — great to meet earlier, and thanks for the thoughtful questions. Short answers up front: 

- Hosted API is the fastest way to get started (no infra, immediate tokens, simple rate limits). It handles bursty traffic well with regional routing and autoscaling, but there are per-tenant rate limits and concurrency controls.
- Dedicated capacity is recommended once you need predictable tail latency, committed throughput, and data isolation (single-tenant GPU pools).
- Private (VPC/on-prem) is typically for regulated customers who need the private control plane and customer-managed networking.

I've attached a short quickstart (redwood-quickstart.pdf) and the Hosted API rate limits table (hosted-api-rate-limits.csv). Below is a minimal curl example you can use to validate latency from your environment: 

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR-API-KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"Summarize the reconciliation report in 2 bullets","max_tokens":60}'

We can issue a short-lived evaluation key for Fintech Co that will give you 100k tokens and a higher default concurrency limit for the first 7 days so you can simulate bursts.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I'll have Rishi (cc'd) create the eval key + a checklist of endpoints and observed limits.
2) You run the quickstart from your network and share any observed tail latencies.
3) If you see variance you don't like, we can schedule a Dedicated sizing call to run a right-sized throughput test.

Attached: redwood-quickstart.pdf, hosted-api-rate-limits.csv

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam@fintech.co>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@fintech.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-22T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation & next steps (quickstart, endpoints, rate limits)

Hi Liam / Sara — following Marissa's note, a few technical clarifications and what I'll provision for the eval: 

- Endpoints: /v1/generate for text, /v1/chat for chat-style structured inputs, /v1/embeddings for vector workloads. All support HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2; zone-aware routing is automatic.
- Rate limits: base account limits are in the CSV, but for the eval I'll raise concurrency to 50 rps and soft throughput to ~1M tokens/day for the 7-day trial so you can stress-test bursts.
- Observability: we'll give you Token-level latency histograms and per-request traces in the Console for the eval period.
- KV/prefix caching: hosted supports prefix caching which will help with repeated template-based requests (useful for reconciliation templates).

When you run the quickstart please capture: 95th/99th percentile token latency, per-request tail latency, and any HTTP 429s. If you hit 429s we can either raise limits for the eval or show how batching/retry backoffs reduce token cost.

I'll also attach an MVP evaluation plan spreadsheet with recommended test cases (mvp-eval-plan.xlsx). If you decide to move to Dedicated later, we can map test results to a Dedicated capacity sizing model.

I'll provision the eval key by EOD Pacific today — Marissa, please confirm billing contact for a potential PO later in the process.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Liam O'Reilly <liam@fintech.co>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@fintech.co>
Date: 2026-02-23T11:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation & next steps (quickstart, endpoints, rate limits)

Thanks both — this looks good. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Token count: our reconciliation job is around 20k tokens per run, and it can run up to 10 parallel jobs during month-end. Will the eval concurrency cover that scenario?
- Data retention: for the eval, can you confirm whether logs/requests are retained in Redwood's Console or if we can opt for client-side masking?

Billing contact for procurement: Rebecca Hall <rebecca.hall@fintech.co> — she'll manage the PO if we move forward.

If the eval concurrency can handle ~200k tokens in a short burst, we'll run the month-end sim next week.

Best,
Liam

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam@fintech.co>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@fintech.co>
Date: 2026-02-25T18:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation & next steps (quickstart, endpoints, rate limits)

Liam — yes, we can cover that. Rishi will bump the eval limits to support ~200k tokens over a short burst (we'll instrument throttles to protect other tenants but the eval keys are raised). Regarding retention: by default Hosted Console stores request logs for 30 days. We can enable client-side masking and redact sensitive fields; for Dedicated/Private you can opt for shorter retention or customer-controlled logging (KMS/HSM options in Private).

Action items: 
- Rishi: provision eval key + raised limits (in progress).
- Liam/Sara: run month-end sim next week and send 95/99 percentile token latency + any 429s.
- Marissa: intro to procurement (Rebecca) and send the Eval Terms (simple SOW & temporary T&Cs).

I'll attach the Eval Terms after this thread. Looking forward to the results.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
